newsitem.title: MALTA: EU says breakthrough made on Greek/Turkish dispute.
newsitem.headline: EU says breakthrough made on Greek/Turkish dispute.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said on Wednesday that Greece and Turkey had made a breakthrough in their dispute over a group of rocky Aegean islets.

"Progress (has been made) in discussions between Greece and Turkey in the problems they have," he told reporters at the end of a two-day meeting of European and Mediterranean foreign ministers which ended here.
"A breakthrough took place today and we shall see the results in the future."
Greece and Turkey have long been at odds over sovereignty of a group of islets in the Aegean and nearly came to blows over the matter last year.
At the time, the then U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher accused the EU of "sleeping through the night" while the crisis unfolded.
The dispute has been blamed for holding up promised European Union funding for a customs union with Turkey.
Van Mierlo admitted the breakthrough had been overshadowed by the Middle East peace crisis, but added:
"We hope for success on this. I don't want to anticipate the results we will have in the next few days, but they will be procedural in nature ... and could lead to a way out".
